requirement:
Setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions MUST
explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose
justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` and author or refresh
its citation review using `habeas author`. The instructions MUST explain that
the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration,
that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception, and that
ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its
target.

text: :::{req} check.exceptions.setup
Setup-generated coverage documentation and bundled agent instructions MUST
explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose
justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor` and author or refresh
its citation review using `habeas author`. The instructions MUST explain that
the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration,
that only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception, and that
ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its
target.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.

output.rationale:
Every clause of `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.setup` specifies what the generated documentation and bundled instructions must say. None prescribes how they are built.

- "explain how to write a standard `habeas:coverage` citation with a prose justification under {cite}`...anchor`" and "author or refresh its citation review using `habeas author`".
- "the anchor requires no project declaration or exception-specific configuration".
- "only current accepted citation evidence permits an exception".
- "ordinary partially uncovered functions need none when their file meets its target".

The clause on how to write the citation and its review names the commands and citation forms the text must explain. It does not require a library, type, signature or delegation. A different build of the same documents would still satisfy the text. For example, the guidance could be stored as a Markdown file instead of a Rust constant. It could be generated by different code, or placed in another bundled skill file. Any of these would produce the same words and still meet the text. So the requirement has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence.

The supplied roots already carry the stated content:
- `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md#section[Habeas]/section[Testing%20and%20coverage%20artifacts]/paragraph@7ca17af232fd` covers every required point:
  - a standard `{cite}` of `habeas:coverage`;
  - rationale in fenced commentary or a Rust doc comment;
  - `habeas author`;
  - no project declaration or extra configuration;
  - only current accepted review evidence permits the exception;
  - partly covered functions need no exception when the file meets its target.
- `md/reference.md#section[How%20it%20works]/section[References]/section[Built-in%20definitions]/paragraph@d87e9cbd9da4` repeats the doc-comment form, the accepted-review rule, and the scope of file and function exceptions.

The setup-generated book text, `src/execution_coverage.rs#const[GUIDANCE]`, also states the same content. It is inserted by `src/execution_coverage/book.rs`. Wording is behavior, so no `{impl}` marker is needed there.

Test edges exist for the content: `tests/repository.rs#fn[shared_agent_guidance_documents_post_suite_checks_and_standard_explanations]`, `tests/setup.rs#fn[coverage_setup_is_idempotent_and_hook_needs_no_coverage_chapter]` and `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]`. I did not read their bodies, so I make no claim about whether they are adequate. That belongs to the behavioral criterion.
